title: Asexual and Sexual Reproduction
seo_title: Grade 8 Asexual and Sexual Reproduction Worksheets: Alleles, Punnett Squares and Variation
standard_text: Develop and use a model to describe why asexual reproduction results in offspring with identical genetic information and sexual reproduction results in offspring with genetic variation.
meta_desc: Free middle school science worksheets on asexual and sexual reproduction (NGSS MS-LS3-2): identical vs. varied offspring, alleles, dominant and recessive traits, and Punnett square probabilities. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: One parent copies; two parents mix.
key_sub: Asexual offspring are genetically identical. Sexual offspring get half their alleles from each parent, which creates variation.
body_html:
How to think about it

Asexual reproduction has one parent. The offspring get a copy of the parent's DNA, so they are genetically identical (bacteria splitting, budding, runners, cuttings).

Sexual reproduction has two parents. Each parent gives half of the chromosomes, one allele for each gene, so offspring have genetic variation.

A Punnett square shows the possible allele combinations. A dominant allele (B) shows its trait with one copy; a recessive trait (bb) shows only with two copies. Each box is 25%.

Example

Bb × Bb: chance of bb?

Bb
BBBBb
bBbbb

1 of 4 boxes is bb.

Answer: 25%

Example

A hydra buds. Offspring's DNA?

One parent.

Answer: identical to the parent

Common mistakes

  • Thinking sexual offspring get all their genes from one parent.
  • Thinking a recessive trait can never appear in offspring of two dominant-looking parents.
  • Reading Bb × Bb as 50% recessive. It is 25%.

faq.q: Why are asexual offspring identical to their parent?
faq.a: They get a copy of all of one parent's genetic information.

faq.q: Why does sexual reproduction create variation?
faq.a: Each parent passes on half of its chromosomes, and different offspring get different combinations of alleles.

faq.q: How do you use a Punnett square?
faq.a: Write one parent's alleles across the top and the other's down the side, fill in each box, and count: each box is a 25% chance.

items.q: Ava reads: “Salmon release eggs and sperm in a stream.” What type of reproduction is this?
items.e: Asexual: one parent. Sexual: two parents (egg and sperm, or pollen and egg).

items.q: What does a dominant allele do?
c: It shows its trait even when only one copy is present.
It needs two copies to show.
items.e: Shown by a capital letter.

items.q: Mia reads: “A hydra grows a bud that breaks off.” How will the offspring's genetic information compare with the parent's?
c: It will be completely random with no parent genes.
It will be a mix of genes from two parents.
It will be identical to the parent's.
items.e: Asexual reproduction copies one parent's DNA; sexual reproduction combines DNA from two parents.
